name: Mobile (Android) Application Testing (OWASP MASTG / MASVS)
description: Comprehensive security testing checklist for Android applications based on OWASP Mobile Application Security Testing Guide (MASTG) and MASVS v2.0.

items.name: Testing Local Data Storage for Sensitive Data
items.how: Inspect app sandbox directories (/data/data/<package>/), SharedPreferences, SQLite databases, internal/external storage, and cache for unencrypted credentials, PII, auth tokens, or private encryption keys.
cases: Inspect /data/data/<package>/shared_prefs/*.xml for plaintext credentials or tokens
Examine SQLite / Room databases in /data/data/<package>/databases/ using sqlite3
Check external storage (SD card / scoped storage) for world-readable application files
Verify whether sensitive cached HTTP responses are saved in cache/ directory
items.expected: No sensitive data (tokens, passwords, PII, keys) stored in plaintext or unencrypted files.
items.recommendation: Use Android Keystore and EncryptedSharedPreferences (AndroidX Security library) for sensitive key/value storage. Encrypt SQLite databases using SQLCipher. Enforce proper file permissions (MODE_PRIVATE).

items.name: Testing Application Backup Configuration (android:allowBackup)
items.how: Verify if android:allowBackup is enabled in AndroidManifest.xml. If enabled, an attacker with physical or USB debugging access can extract full application private data via 'adb backup'.
cases: Decompile AndroidManifest.xml and check if android:allowBackup='true'
Attempt adb backup -f backup.ab -noapk {{PACKAGE}} and extract with abe.jar
items.expected: android:allowBackup is set to 'false' or strict full-backup-content rules are defined.
items.recommendation: Set android:allowBackup="false" in AndroidManifest.xml unless backup is explicitly required. If required, implement strict backup_rules.xml excluding private databases, keystores, and shared_prefs.
items.command_template: adb shell dumpsys package {{PACKAGE}} | grep -i flags

items.name: Testing Sensitive Data in Logs (Logcat)
mitre_technique: T1413 - Access Sensitive Data in System Logs
items.how: Monitor Android system logs (Logcat) while interacting with authentication, payments, profile edits, and sensitive transactions to detect leaking credentials, session tokens, or PII.
cases: Run adb logcat while authenticating and performing API requests
Search logs for passwords, JWT tokens, session IDs, credit cards, or internal error stack traces
items.expected: Production release builds must not output sensitive parameters, credentials, or PII to system logs.
items.recommendation: Remove all Log.d(), Log.v(), and System.out.println() statements in production builds using ProGuard/R8 release rules (e.g. -assumenosideeffects class android.util.Log { *; }).

items.name: Testing Memory for Sensitive Data & Heap Dumps
items.how: Capture an Android runtime process heap dump using 'am dumpheap' or Frida and inspect memory strings for unencrypted passwords, encryption keys, and session tokens lingering indefinitely.
cases: Authenticate in the application and perform critical actions
Dump process heap to disk via adb shell am dumpheap
Convert hprof with hprof-conv and search memory strings for credentials
items.expected: Sensitive credentials are wiped from memory immediately after use (using char[] arrays instead of immutable java.lang.String).
items.recommendation: Store passwords and encryption keys in char[] or byte[] arrays and overwrite them with zeroes (Arrays.fill) immediately after use.
items.command_template: adb shell am dumpheap {{PACKAGE}} /data/local/tmp/heap.hprof && adb pull /data/local/tmp/heap.hprof

items.name: Testing for Insecure or Broken Cryptographic Algorithms
items.how: Analyze decompiled Java/Kotlin source and native libraries for weak cryptographic algorithms like MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RC4, or AES in ECB mode.
cases: Search decompiled code for Cipher.getInstance("AES/ECB") or "DES"
Search for MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5") or "SHA-1" for security-critical checks
Verify IV (Initialization Vector) randomness: ensure static or hardcoded IVs are not used
items.expected: Strong algorithms (AES-GCM-256, ChaCha20-Poly1305, SHA-256+, RSA 2048+) with cryptographically secure random IVs.
items.recommendation: Use AES-GCM or AES-CBC with HMAC-SHA256. Use SecureRandom for IV generation. Do not use ECB mode or broken hashing algorithms (MD5/SHA1).

items.name: Testing for Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys & Secrets
items.how: Search decompiled classes, assets, strings.xml, and native .so libraries for hardcoded AES/HMAC keys, private certificates, AWS/Firebase keys, and API secrets.
cases: Decompile APK with JADX and search strings for private keys and tokens
Run trufflehog / gitleaks against decompiled codebase
Inspect native binaries (.so) with 'strings' and 'rabin2'
items.expected: No static cryptographic keys or backend secrets hardcoded within the APK bundle.
items.recommendation: Use Android Keystore for client-side cryptographic key generation and storage. Store third-party backend secrets on a secure server, not within the client application.

items.name: Testing Android KeyStore Usage and Key Protection
items.how: Verify that cryptographic keys are generated inside the Android KeyStore provider with hardware-backed security (TEE / StrongBox) and proper user authentication requirements.
cases: Check if KeyStore provider is initialized with KeyGenParameterSpec
Verify if setUserAuthenticationRequired(true) is used for biometric-bound keys
Inspect KeyStore aliases with Objection
items.expected: Keys generated in Android KeyStore (AndroidKeyStore provider) and protected with StrongBox/TEE when available.
items.recommendation: Use AndroidKeyStore provider with KeyProperties.PURPOSE_ENCRYPT | KeyProperties.PURPOSE_DECRYPT and setIsStrongBoxBacked(true) where available.

items.name: Testing Network Security Configuration & Cleartext Traffic
items.how: Check res/xml/network_security_config.xml and AndroidManifest.xml for android:usesCleartextTraffic='true' or domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted='true'.
cases: Inspect AndroidManifest.xml for android:usesCleartextTraffic='true'
Review network_security_config.xml for insecure base-config or domain-config rules
Verify all network calls use HTTPS with TLS 1.2/1.3
items.expected: Cleartext HTTP traffic is completely disabled (cleartextTrafficPermitted='false'). All endpoints enforce HTTPS.
items.recommendation: Set android:usesCleartextTraffic="false" and configure network_security_config.xml to forbid cleartext communication across all domains.
items.command_template: cat ./jadx_out/resources/res/xml/network_security_config.xml 2>/dev/null || echo "No custom network security config found"

items.name: Testing SSL / TLS Certificate Pinning & Pinning Bypass
items.how: Verify if the application implements SSL/TLS certificate pinning (via Network Security Config pin-set, OkHttp CertificatePinner, or TrustKit). Test resilience against pinning bypass via Frida / Objection.
cases: Intercept traffic using Burp Suite proxy with user-installed CA cert
Check if app refuses connections without pinning bypass
Run Objection / Frida pinning bypass script to test hookability
items.expected: Certificate pinning is implemented on all critical API domains and validates public key hashes (SPKI pins).
items.recommendation: Implement pin-set in network_security_config.xml or use OkHttp CertificatePinner with primary and backup backup public key hashes.

items.name: Testing Exported Activities and Intent Spoofing
items.how: Inspect AndroidManifest.xml for exported activities (android:exported='true' or implicit intent-filters without explicit android:exported='false'). Trigger exported activities directly using 'am start' to bypass authentication.
cases: List all exported activities using aapt / jadx
Trigger internal / dashboard activities via adb shell am start
Verify if authentication check can be bypassed
items.expected: Internal activities are set to android:exported='false' or protected with strong custom signature permissions.
items.recommendation: Explicitly declare android:exported="false" on all activities that should not be invoked by external apps. Require signature-level permissions for inter-app communication.

items.name: Testing Exported Content Providers & Injection Flaws
items.how: Query exported content providers via adb or drozer to inspect if unauthorized apps can read or modify internal app databases, or inject SQL payloads through URI query parameters.
cases: Query content provider URIs via adb shell content query
Test SQL injection in selection arguments: --where "1=1"
Check path traversal in openFile() implementation
items.expected: Content providers are not exported unless necessary, and enforce parameterized queries and path sanitization.
items.recommendation: Set android:exported="false" on content providers. If export is required, protect with signature permissions and sanitize all file paths / SQL arguments.

items.name: Testing Deep Links and Custom URL Schemes
items.how: Review custom URI schemes (e.g. myapp://) and App Links in AndroidManifest.xml. Test if malicious web pages or external apps can trigger sensitive actions, CSRF, account takeovers, or open redirects.
cases: Extract all custom URL scheme handlers from AndroidManifest.xml
Trigger deep links with malicious parameters via adb shell am start -d "scheme://path?param=payload"
Verify if deep link actions require active session verification
items.expected: Deep links validate origin, enforce state tokens for authentication handshakes, and use verified Android App Links (assetlinks.json) instead of unverified custom URL schemes.
items.recommendation: Migrate from custom schemes to verified Android App Links (autoVerify='true'). Sanitize all incoming deep link parameters and never perform sensitive actions (transfers, auth state changes) automatically without user confirmation.

items.name: Testing Root Detection and Bypass Mechanisms
items.how: Verify if the app detects rooted devices (checking su binaries, test-keys, Magisk packages, RootBeer library) and test how easily root detection can be hooked and bypassed using Frida / Objection.
cases: Launch application on rooted device and inspect warning / termination behavior
Execute Objection root bypass command to test bypassability
Check if native C/C++ checks or SafetyNet / Play Integrity API are utilized
items.expected: App implements multi-layered root detection using both Java and native C checks, and verifies device integrity with Google Play Integrity API.
items.recommendation: Implement multi-layered root checks (file system, system properties, native checks) combined with Google Play Integrity API server-side token validation.

items.name: Testing Code Obfuscation and Debuggable Flag
items.how: Verify that android:debuggable='false' in production builds, and verify that ProGuard / R8 / DexGuard is enabled to obfuscate class, method, and variable names.
cases: Check if android:debuggable='true' via aapt dump badging
Decompile APK with JADX and check if class and method names are minified (e.g. a.b.c)
items.expected: android:debuggable is false. Source code is minified and obfuscated with ProGuard / R8.
items.recommendation: Ensure minifyEnabled true and shrinkResources true in build.gradle for release builds. Never ship debuggable builds in production.
